summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with hands-on embedded software experience in C and C++ across STM32 microcontrollers, Arduino, and NVIDIA Jetson platforms. Built bare-metal firmware with FreeRTOS task scheduling and UART/I2C/SPI peripheral drivers, debugging and verifying behavior on Cortex-M4 hardware with Proteus. Uses Git for version control and Python for hardware-integration tooling across embedded and robotics projects.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi over I2C and translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands in Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; debugged and resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.
Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination on STM32, integrating VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART command handling and user override on STM32.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built a Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.

Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) with interrupt-driven sample capture and a low-level I2C driver; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate, with functional validation in Proteus.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++, driving five servos with range-gated contact detection via dual VL53L0X ToF sensors.
Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) through systematic debugging; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Deployed the Jetson-side controller as an auto-restarting systemd service with static IP networking for reliable multi-device communication.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
